description: Mobile proxy IP rotation health — pool cycling, stuck proxies, rotation success rate, and per-server breakdown

panels.description: Total number of unique proxy devices that recorded at least one periodic rotation attempt in the selected time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT proxy_id) AS value
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )

panels.title: Total proxies

panels.description: Percentage of periodic rotation attempts where ip_after differed from ip_before (i.e. the IP actually changed). Lower values indicate systemic rotation failure.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(success) / COUNT(*), 1) AS value
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )

panels.title: Rotation success rate

panels.description: Proxies that received multiple rotation commands but their ip_before never changed — the carrier keeps assigning the same address.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM (
  SELECT proxy_id
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1
) t

panels.title: Stuck proxies (1 IP only)

panels.description: Proxies whose entire observed IP pool contains only 2–5 unique addresses. They rotate, but within a tiny fixed set — predictable and fingerprintable.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM (
  SELECT proxy_id
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5
) t

panels.title: Small-pool cycling (2–5 IPs)

panels.description: Proxies that have been assigned 5+ distinct IPs over the period. These are working as intended — the carrier is allocating freely from its pool.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM (
  SELECT proxy_id
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) > 5
) t

panels.title: Healthy proxies (5+ IPs)

panels.description: Average time in milliseconds from when the rotation command was sent to when the new IP was verified. High values indicate slow airplane-mode cycles or carrier reconnect delays.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(rotation_duration_ms), 0) AS value
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  AND rotation_duration_ms IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Avg rotation duration

panels.description: Distribution of proxies by IP pool size category over the selected period. Stuck = 1 IP only; Cycling = 2–5 IPs; Medium = 6–20 IPs; Healthy = 20+ IPs.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  pool_group                AS metric,
  CAST(COUNT(*) AS SIGNED)  AS value
FROM (
  SELECT
    proxy_id,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1              THEN 'Stuck (1 IP)'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5  THEN 'Cycling (2-5 IPs)'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'Medium (6-20 IPs)'
      ELSE 'Healthy (20+ IPs)'
    END AS pool_group
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
) t
GROUP BY pool_group
ORDER BY FIELD(pool_group,
  'Stuck (1 IP)', 'Cycling (2-5 IPs)', 'Medium (6-20 IPs)', 'Healthy (20+ IPs)')

panels.title: IP pool size distribution

panels.description: Cities with the highest concentration of stuck or cycling proxies (pool size ≤ 5). Helps identify geographic clusters that may share a problem carrier node or DHCP pool.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.city')) AS metric,
  COUNT(DISTINCT proxy_id) AS value
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  AND JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.city') IS NOT NULL
  AND proxy_id IN (
    SELECT proxy_id
    FROM ip_rotations
    WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
    GROUP BY proxy_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) <= 5
  )
GROUP BY metric
ORDER BY value DESC
LIMIT 15

panels.title: Stuck + cycling proxies by city (top 15)

panels.description: Average rotation duration broken down by pool health group. Stuck proxies typically show higher durations because the verification timeout fires before a new IP appears.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT pool_group, ROUND(AVG(avg_duration), 0) AS avg_duration_ms
FROM (
  SELECT proxy_id,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1             THEN 'Stuck'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5  THEN 'Cycling'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'Medium'
      ELSE 'Healthy'
    END AS pool_group,
    AVG(rotation_duration_ms) AS avg_duration
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
    AND rotation_duration_ms IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY proxy_id
) t
GROUP BY pool_group
ORDER BY FIELD(pool_group, 'Stuck', 'Cycling', 'Medium', 'Healthy')

panels.title: Avg rotation duration by pool group (ms)

panels.description: Count of periodic rotation attempts over time split by outcome. A rising 'failed' line indicates a worsening rotation problem across the fleet.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(rotation_timestamp, $__interval),
  SUM(success)     AS success,
  SUM(1 - success) AS failed
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE $__timeFilter(rotation_timestamp)
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Rotation attempts over time — success vs failed

panels.description: Count of rotation events where ip_before = ip_after, meaning the device reconnected to the exact same IP. This is the raw signal for stuck behaviour.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(rotation_timestamp, $__interval),
  COUNT(*) AS same_ip_count
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE $__timeFilter(rotation_timestamp)
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  AND ip_before = ip_after
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Same-IP rotations over time (ip_before = ip_after)

panels.description: Each server's proxy count broken down by pool health group (Stuck / Cycling / Medium / Healthy). Servers dominated by red/orange bars need investigation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  server_name,
  pool_group,
  COUNT(*) AS proxy_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    proxy_id,
    CASE
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name')))))
           REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
      THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(
             UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name'))))),
             '^S[0-9]{1,3}'
           )
      ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
    END AS server_name,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1              THEN 'Stuck'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5  THEN 'Cycling'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'Medium'
      ELSE 'Healthy'
    END AS pool_group
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
) classified
GROUP BY server_name, pool_group
ORDER BY server_name,
  FIELD(pool_group, 'Stuck', 'Cycling', 'Medium', 'Healthy')

panels.title: Proxy pool health by server

panels.description: Per-server summary: total proxies, stuck and cycling counts, percentage of problematic proxies, and average rotation success rate. Sorted by worst performers first.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  server_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT proxy_id)                                                        AS total_proxies,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Stuck'   THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                        AS stuck_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Cycling' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                        AS cycling_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Healthy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                        AS healthy_count,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group IN ('Stuck','Cycling') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    / COUNT(DISTINCT proxy_id), 1
  )                                                                               AS pct_stuck_cycling,
  ROUND(AVG(success_rate), 1)                                                     AS success_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    proxy_id,
    CASE
      WHEN UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name')))))
           REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
      THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(
             UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name'))))),
             '^S[0-9]{1,3}'
           )
      ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
    END AS server_name,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1              THEN 'Stuck'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5  THEN 'Cycling'
      WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'Medium'
      ELSE 'Healthy'
    END AS pool_group,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(success), 1) AS success_rate
  FROM ip_rotations
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
  GROUP BY proxy_id
) classified
GROUP BY server_name
ORDER BY pct_stuck_cycling DESC

panels.title: Server risk table

panels.description: Full list of proxies with a small fixed IP pool (2–5 IPs). Shows the exact cycle sequence each proxy rotates through, how many rotations were attempted, and the success rate.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  ir.proxy_id,
  MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(ir.device_metadata, '$.name')))    AS device_name,
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(ir.device_metadata, '$.city'))), ''),
    ', ',
    COALESCE(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(ir.device_metadata, '$.state'))), '')
  )                                                                  AS location,
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(ir.device_metadata, '$.name')))))
         REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
    THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(
           UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(ir.device_metadata, '$.name'))))),
           '^S[0-9]{1,3}'
         )
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
  END                                                                AS server_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ir.ip_before)                                       AS pool_size,
  COUNT(*)                                                           AS total_rotations,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(ir.success), 1)                                 AS success_rate_pct,
  GROUP_CONCAT(
    DISTINCT ir.ip_before
    ORDER BY ir.ip_before
    SEPARATOR ' -> '
  )                                                                  AS ip_cycle
FROM ip_rotations ir
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
GROUP BY ir.proxy_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ir.ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5
ORDER BY total_rotations DESC

panels.title: Small-pool cycling proxies — full detail

panels.description: Proxies that have never changed IP during the selected window. Shows the locked IP address, which /16 subnet it belongs to, total rotation attempts, and how long the proxy has been stuck.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  proxy_id,
  MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name')))   AS device_name,
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.city'))), ''),
    ', ',
    COALESCE(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.state'))), '')
  )                                                              AS location,
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name')))))
         REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
    THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(
           UPPER(TRIM(MAX(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(device_metadata, '$.name'))))),
           '^S[0-9]{1,3}'
         )
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
  END                                                            AS server_name,
  MIN(ip_before)                                                 AS locked_ip,
  SUBSTRING_INDEX(MIN(ip_before), '.', 2)                       AS ip_16_block,
  COUNT(*)                                                       AS total_rotations,
  ROUND(
    TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, MIN(rotation_timestamp), MAX(rotation_timestamp)) / 60.0,
    1
  )                                                              AS hours_stuck
FROM ip_rotations
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
GROUP BY proxy_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1
ORDER BY hours_stuck DESC

panels.title: Stuck proxies — never changed IP

panels.description: Groups proxies by their first two IP octets (/16 block) and shows how many in each subnet are Stuck, Cycling, Medium, or Healthy. Subnets with high stuck counts indicate carrier-level DHCP pool exhaustion or business account IP reservation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  SUBSTRING_INDEX(ip_before, '.', 2)           AS ip_16_block,
  COUNT(DISTINCT proxy_id)                      AS total_proxies,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Stuck'    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS stuck_proxies,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Cycling'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cycling_proxies,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Medium'   THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS medium_proxies,
  SUM(CASE WHEN pool_group = 'Healthy'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS healthy_proxies
FROM (
  /* Step 2 – attach pool_group label to every row */
  SELECT t.proxy_id, t.ip_before, g.pool_group
  FROM ip_rotations t
  JOIN (
    /* Step 1 – classify each proxy by its unique-IP count */
    SELECT proxy_id,
      CASE
        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) = 1             THEN 'Stuck'
        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 2 AND 5  THEN 'Cycling'
        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT ip_before) BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'Medium'
        ELSE 'Healthy'
      END AS pool_group
    FROM ip_rotations
    WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
    GROUP BY proxy_id
  ) g ON g.proxy_id = t.proxy_id
  WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
) classified
GROUP BY ip_16_block
HAVING total_proxies >= 3
ORDER BY stuck_proxies DESC
LIMIT 30

panels.title: Problem subnets — /16 breakdown (stuck vs healthy)

panels.description: Breakdown of rotation events by rotation_type (e.g. standard, manual, scheduled). All panels in this dashboard filter to periodic only — this chart shows the split within that subset.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(rc.cycle_type, 'unknown')   AS cycle_type,
  COALESCE(ir.rotation_type, 'unknown') AS rotation_type,
  COUNT(*)                              AS total_rotations,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(ir.success), 1)    AS success_rate_pct
FROM ip_rotations ir
LEFT JOIN xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles rc ON rc.id = ir.cycle_id
WHERE rotation_timestamp >= $__timeFrom() AND rotation_timestamp <= $__timeTo()
  AND cycle_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM xproxy_tester.rotation_cycles
    WHERE cycle_type = 'periodic'
    AND $__timeFilter(cycle_timestamp)
  )
GROUP BY rc.cycle_type, ir.rotation_type
ORDER BY total_rotations DESC

SELECT DISTINCT
  CASE WHEN UPPER(TRIM(name)) REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
    THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '^S[0-9]{1,3}')
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN' END AS __text,
  CASE WHEN UPPER(TRIM(name)) REGEXP '^S[0-9]{1,3}(P[0-9]+|[[:space:]_-]+P[0-9]+)'
    THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(UPPER(TRIM(name)), '^S[0-9]{1,3}')
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN' END AS __value
FROM proxies
GROUP BY __text, __value
ORDER BY CASE WHEN __value = 'UNKNOWN' THEN 999999
  ELSE CAST(SUBSTRING(__value, 2) AS UNSIGNED) END
